---
title: "How to localize a probe while SpikeGLX records"
---

This guide runs the ephys-only localizer during a SpikeGLX acquisition of a Neuropixels probe
(1.0; 2.0, single- or four-shank, see [Other probes](#other-probes)). Every 10 s it takes the
5 s of AP and LF data just acquired, computes the channel
features, and re-estimates where each channel is, starting from the planned trajectory (a plan
file, or a Pinpoint export) or, without one, searching the whole brain. A window shows the
estimate and the plan on atlas slices, with the region of every channel.

::: {.callout-warning}
Experimental (branch `realtime-localization-w45`). It has been validated by replaying IBL
recordings, not yet during a live experiment: run it alongside your usual workflow rather than
to guide an insertion.
:::

## Prerequisites

- Windows, with SpikeGLX acquiring a Neuropixels probe: a 1.0 with its LF band (what the
  localizer was fitted on), or a 2.0 (experimental, see [Other probes](#other-probes)). It also
  works on a recording that SpikeGLX plays back as a simulated probe.
- Python 3.12 or later, and about 4 GB of free RAM per feature worker: the viewer starts as many
  workers as the free RAM allows (3 keep up with a snippet every 10 s).
- Internet on the first run: the channel model (Hugging Face Hub) and the Allen atlas download
  automatically.

## Install

1. ibleatools on the real-time branch (the [lite install](../explanation/install-variants.qmd)
   is enough):

    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/int-brain-lab/ibleatools
    cd ibleatools
    git checkout realtime-localization-w45
    python -m venv .venv
    .venv\Scripts\activate
    pip install -e .
    ```

2. The fitted localizer (3 MB):
   download `ephys-only-fit-2026_W45_lf_ap_no_detection.zip` from the
   [`localizer-2026_W45` release](https://github.com/alonsaguy/probe-viewer/releases/tag/localizer-2026_W45)
   and unzip it into `%USERPROFILE%\ephys-atlas\results\alignment\`, which gives

    ```
    %USERPROFILE%\ephys-atlas\results\alignment\ephys_only_fit\32b2d91a88c38cc89299e24c0bac0ed000a49c1d_lf_ap_no_detection\
        fit.npz  fit_summary.json  grid.npz  temperature_tuning.csv
    ```

   (to keep results elsewhere, set `EPHYS_ATLAS_RESULTS_DIR` to the folder that holds
   `alignment\`). Without these files the localizer fits itself on first use, which needs the
   IBL feature release and IBL database credentials.

3. The SpikeGLX SDK: download the [SpikeGLX-CPP-SDK](https://github.com/billkarsh/SpikeGLX-CPP-SDK)
   (Code / Download ZIP) and unzip it into `%USERPROFILE%\SpikeGLX\`, which gives
   `%USERPROFILE%\SpikeGLX\SpikeGLX-CPP-SDK-main\`. Copy `Windows\API\SglxApi.dll` into
   `Windows\Python\sglx_pkg\`. (Elsewhere: set `SGLX_SDK_DIR` to its `Windows\Python` folder.)

4. In SpikeGLX: **Options / Command Server Settings**, enable the command server (port 4142).

## The plan

The localizer is most accurate starting from the planned trajectory (see
[What to expect](#what-to-expect)). It reads it from one of:

- a **Pinpoint export**: the experiment JSON that [Pinpoint](https://pinpoint.allenneuraldynamics.org)
  v5 saves, planned in its `allen_mouse` or `qiu2018_mouse` atlas. Pass the file with `--plan`
  and, when it holds several probes, the probe with `--plan-probe "Probe A"`. Plans in the
  `qiu2018_mouse` (MRI) atlas are mapped to the Allen CCF with the scaling of iblatlas'
  `MRITorontoAtlas` (an affine approximation);
- a **plan file** made from the insertion's entry point and angles, in the IBL convention (the
  one of the Alyx trajectories):

    ```python
    from ephysatlas.realtime.plan import plan_from_trajectory, save_plan

    plan = plan_from_trajectory(x=-1200, y=-2000, z=0, depth=4000, theta=15, phi=180)
    save_plan(plan, r"C:\data\plan.json")
    ```

    `x`, `y`, `z`: entry point in µm from bregma (ML, AP, DV); `depth`: insertion depth along
    the probe in µm; `theta`: angle from vertical in degrees; `phi`: azimuth in degrees. The
    numbers above are an example. For an IBL insertion (with IBL database credentials),
    `plan_from_alyx(pid)` reads the planned trajectory from Alyx.

Without a plan, every update searches the whole brain instead: it scores ~230,000 straight
trajectories (400 µm apart, 10-30° from vertical, every 30° of azimuth), takes the five best
that are at least 1 mm apart on average, refines each one and keeps the best.

## Run

Start a SpikeGLX run, then, in the ibleatools folder with the environment activated, one of:

```bash
python scripts\realtime_viewer.py --sglx --plan C:\data\experiment-001.json --plan-probe "Probe A"
python scripts\realtime_viewer.py --sglx --plan C:\data\plan.json
python scripts\realtime_viewer.py --sglx
```

(the last one without a plan: whole-brain search).

- `--probe N`: the imec probe index in SpikeGLX (default 0), one probe per viewer; for several
  probes, run one viewer per probe, each with its `--probe` and its `--plan-probe`.
- `--shank N`: on a four-shank probe, the shank to localize (default: the one recording the
  most channels); run one viewer per shank to localize several.
- `--sglx ADDRESS`: SpikeGLX on another computer, or a command server bound to a network address
  (the address the Command Server Settings dialog shows). Running the localizer on a second
  computer keeps its CPU load off the acquisition machine.
- `--workers N`, `--cadence S`: feature workers, seconds between snippets (default 10).

Close the window to stop; the run is saved in
`%USERPROFILE%\ephys-atlas\results\realtime\viewer_runs\`.

To try it without a probe, let SpikeGLX play one of your Neuropixels 1.0 recordings as a
simulated probe, start the run and use the same command.

## What to expect {#what-to-expect}

- A snippet's features take about 25 s per worker; with enough workers the estimate updates
  every 10 s, about 30 s behind the acquisition. With fewer, snippets are skipped so that the
  estimate always uses recent data. Localizing takes about 1 s from a plan and about 9 s without
  one; without a plan, the console lists each update's five candidates (score, position,
  regions) and the window's status line the one kept.
- The estimate after one snippet is about as good as after five minutes.
- On 196 held-out IBL insertions (medians): 536 µm from the histology-based alignment, against
  754 µm for the plan; Cosmos region accuracy 0.74 (plan 0.57), Beryl 0.35 (plan 0.21).
- Without a plan, on 20 of these insertions (medians): 658 µm from the histology, against 485 µm
  for the search from the plan and 907 µm for the plan itself. It is closer to the histology than
  the plan for 11 of the 20 but more than 1.5 mm off for 4, and the hemisphere cannot be told
  (the estimate is shown in the left one): use a plan when there is one.
- Plans off by up to ~0.25 mm or 10° cost nothing; a plan 1 mm or more off is only partly
  corrected. The model assumes the probe is 10-30° from vertical, tip down, as in the IBL
  insertions it was fitted on.
- The Open Ephys version of the same localizer (a Probe Viewer plugin,
  [`alonsaguy/probe-viewer`](https://github.com/alonsaguy/probe-viewer), branch
  `realtime-localization`) runs in C++ with the same whole-brain search and Pinpoint reader
  (Neuropixels 1.0 only).

## Other probes {#other-probes}

The localizer was fitted on Neuropixels 1.0 recordings (bank 0: 384 channels over 3.84 mm,
with an LF band). Other probes run, one shank at a time, but **how accurate it is on them has
not been measured**: treat the estimate as a rough indication.

- **Neuropixels 2.0** (single-shank NP2000/NP2003, four-shank NP2010/NP2013/NP2014, quad base
  NP2020): these record one wideband signal, so the LF band is derived from it (low-passed at
  1 kHz and decimated to 2.5 kHz, as IBL does for its 2.0 recordings).
- **One shank at a time**: on a four-shank probe the viewer localizes one shank (`--shank`,
  default the one recording the most channels) from that shank's channels only. The window
  says which shank and how many channels.
- **Any channel map**: the shank's channels are resampled by depth onto rows 10 µm apart over
  the span they record, so other banks and IMRO tables work. The probe length the localizer
  expects is scaled to that span. A shank recording less than ~1 mm (e.g. 96 channels per
  shank across four shanks) gives a short trajectory that is harder to place; a few hundred
  µm is the minimum.
- **Plans**: a plan file made with `plan_from_trajectory` or from Alyx is read as the line of
  the localized shank. A Pinpoint plan of a 2.0 uses that probe's own contacts, but its line
  runs through the shank Pinpoint positions (shank 0 unless set otherwise). For another shank
  the 250 µm per shank lateral offset is not applied; the viewer prints a warning when this
  happens.
- The saved run (`updates.npz`) also holds `recorded_channel_xyz`, the estimated position of
  each recorded channel of the shank, with `recorded_channels`, their SpikeGLX channel indices.
